description.value: Oni-Oni is a Japanese confectionery shop opened in March 2021 by a local Japanese-Canadian family, specializing in fresh-made onigiri (nori-wrapped rice triangles) with a wide array of fillings, alongside kakigori (Japanese shaved ice), imported Japanese snacks, candy, and soft drinks. The quick-service, grab-and-go format makes it an ideal mid-ride fuel stop for cyclists passing through Victoria's Johnson Street. The shop is run by the same family behind Sakura Sushi and OTAKI, and gift cards are redeemable across all three locations.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is fully available and confirms address (585 Johnson ST, Victoria BC), business type (Japanese confectionery and snack shop, takeout-oriented), and menu items. No phone number is displayed in website text (contact page shows a form only), so phone is unconfirmed. No evidence on the website for bike parking, washrooms, Wi-Fi, or other cyclist amenities. Several menu items list plant-based ingredients explicitly, supporting a vegetarian value=true.
concerns: Phone number (+1 778 432-0664) from OSM is not displayed anywhere in the website text (contact page only shows a submission form), so it could not be verified or contradicted.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active, publicly accessible Japanese confectionery and snack shop in central Victoria. Ideal quick-stop for touring cyclists seeking portable, affordable food.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Multiple onigiri fillings are explicitly plant-based per listed ingredients: Plain, Goma & Kombu (sesame seed with preserved seaweed), Ume Shiso (pickled plum with shiso leaves), Natto Negi (fermented soybeans with scallions), Takana (pickled mustard greens), Garlic Sesame. No GF or vegan labeling confirmed
